title: Quick to Confess
summary: Jesus knew all our sin when he saved us. Sin puts distance between us and him, so be quick to confess and return.
exhortation: When Jesus saved us, he knew all of our sin: past, present and future. Even though we don't know the depths of our own sin, Jesus knew and knows. That should make us quick to run to him and confess.

When we confess our sin, we're admitting that we've broken his law and wronged him. We're also confessing our weakness and our need. So my encouragement this morning is that we would be quick to see the great grace displayed on the cross, and that it would make us quick to confess and be made right in our hearts toward Jesus.

When we sin, it doesn't sever our relationship with him, but it does put distance in it. And remember, it isn't God who distanced himself from us. Jesus didn't recoil or walk away. We put the distance there. When we do, we just need to confess and return, find forgiveness for our sin, and find the strength and grace to get up and follow him.
prayer: Lord, may we be quick to run to you: quick to repent, quick to confess, quick to seek forgiveness. You have stored up an endless reserve of mercy so that we might be forgiven.
So may we run to you and to your cross this morning, where forgiveness and mercy are new. In Jesus' name, amen.
